title: Sleep & recovery — when, not how much
description: The Oura app already shows nightly averages. This shows where inside the night they came from.

panels.title: HRV across the night, one line per night
panels.description: Aligned on each night's own bedtime rather than the clock, so a night that started before midnight is comparable with one that started at 3 a.m. Gaps are gaps — the ring produced no reading, and nothing is interpolated across them.

targets.rawSql:
select
    timestamptz '1970-01-01 00:00:00+00'
        + make_interval(secs => extract(epoch from (ts - first_value(ts) over (partition by night order by ts)))) as "time",
    to_char(night, 'Mon DD') as metric,
    value
from sleep_series
where metric = 'hrv'
  and $__timeFilter(ts)
-- Must be time-ascending: Grafana rejects an unsorted frame when pivoting the
-- `metric` column into one series per night.
order by 1, night

panels.title: HRV heatmap — night × time into night
panels.description: Each column is one night, each row a 30-minute band from bedtime. Reads as a map of when recovery collapses rather than whether the average was good.

targets.rawSql:
select
    night::timestamptz as "time",
    round(avg(value) filter (where band = 0)::numeric, 1) as "0.5",
    round(avg(value) filter (where band = 1)::numeric, 1) as "1.0",
    round(avg(value) filter (where band = 2)::numeric, 1) as "1.5",
    round(avg(value) filter (where band = 3)::numeric, 1) as "2.0",
    round(avg(value) filter (where band = 4)::numeric, 1) as "2.5",
    round(avg(value) filter (where band = 5)::numeric, 1) as "3.0",
    round(avg(value) filter (where band = 6)::numeric, 1) as "3.5",
    round(avg(value) filter (where band = 7)::numeric, 1) as "4.0",
    round(avg(value) filter (where band = 8)::numeric, 1) as "4.5",
    round(avg(value) filter (where band = 9)::numeric, 1) as "5.0",
    round(avg(value) filter (where band = 10)::numeric, 1) as "5.5",
    round(avg(value) filter (where band = 11)::numeric, 1) as "6.0",
    round(avg(value) filter (where band = 12)::numeric, 1) as "6.5",
    round(avg(value) filter (where band = 13)::numeric, 1) as "7.0",
    round(avg(value) filter (where band = 14)::numeric, 1) as "7.5",
    round(avg(value) filter (where band = 15)::numeric, 1) as "8.0",
    round(avg(value) filter (where band = 16)::numeric, 1) as "8.5",
    round(avg(value) filter (where band = 17)::numeric, 1) as "9.0",
    round(avg(value) filter (where band = 18)::numeric, 1) as "9.5",
    round(avg(value) filter (where band = 19)::numeric, 1) as "10.0"
from (
    select
        night,
        value,
        -- Half-hour bands measured from each night's own bedtime, so a night that
        -- began at 00:07 lines up with one that began at 03:00.
        floor(
            extract(epoch from (ts - first_value(ts) over (partition by night order by ts))) / 1800
        )::int as band
    from sleep_series
    where metric = 'hrv'
      and value is not null
      and $__timeFilter(ts)
) banded
group by night
order by night

panels.title: Hypnogram
panels.description: One cell per 5 minutes. Read against the heart rate below it: a REM block with a rising heart rate is a different night from a REM block without one.

targets.rawSql:
select
    ts as "time",
    case phase
        when 1 then 'Deep'
        when 2 then 'Light'
        when 3 then 'REM'
        when 4 then 'Awake'
    end as "Sleep phase"
from hypnogram
where $__timeFilter(ts)
order by ts

panels.title: Heart rate and HRV during sleep
panels.description: The 5-minute arrays as they actually arrive, on the clock. lowest_heart_rate in `daily` is computed by Oura on 30-second samples and will not equal the minimum of this line — that discrepancy is expected.

targets.rawSql:
select
    ts as "time",
    case metric when 'hr' then 'Heart rate' else 'HRV' end as metric,
    value
from sleep_series
where $__timeFilter(ts)
order by ts

panels.title: Per-night coverage
panels.description: How much of each night the ring actually measured. A night with many gaps makes its averages less trustworthy, and nothing else on this page tells you that.

targets.rawSql:
select
    night as "Night",
    round(extract(epoch from (last_ts - first_ts)) / 3600.0, 1) as "Hours",
    samples as "Cells",
    gaps as "Gaps",
    round(100.0 * gaps / nullif(samples + gaps, 0), 1) as "Gap %",
    round(avg_value::numeric, 1) as "Mean HRV",
    round(median_value::numeric, 1) as "Median HRV",
    round(min_value::numeric, 1) as "Min HRV",
    round(max_value::numeric, 1) as "Max HRV"
from sleep_nightly
where metric = 'hrv'
  and $__timeFilter(first_ts)
order by night desc
